rv.q: But this play, like its characters, has a good deal going for it, especially five rich roles for young women acted with compassion, humor and heartbreak by an excellent ensemble.

Unfortunately, much of the rest of the content deals with the more conventional stuff of a bildungsroman, with the girls dealing with matters of self-discovery, friendship, competitiveness, and sexuality.
Carr’s clever script builds slowly as we learn more about each girl, then all at once as the teens deal with a crisis that binds together their religious convictions and FFA duties.

cn.t: Critics find Carr's rodeo-set drama about five Texas teens features an original premise and humane character work, though the execution doesn't fully deliver on its promising setup.

vr.q: Despite a relatively slow start, the play has lovely character development and covers a lot of ground in just 90 minutes.
